title: How Much Water Is on Earth, Really?
lines: How much water is there on Earth, really?
Oceans cover seventy-one percent of the planet.
Now gather every drop: | the oceans, the ice caps, the lakes, the rivers, even the clouds.
Pull it all together into one ball.
It would be just one thousand three hundred eighty-five kilometers across.
That's less than half the width of the Moon.
Next to Earth, it's a small blue bead.
Now keep only the liquid fresh water: | the lakes, the rivers, the swamps, the groundwater.
That ball is just two hundred seventy-three kilometers wide.
And the water in every lake and river on the planet?
A tiny drop, about fifty-six kilometers across. | Roughly the width of London.
That's what so much of life depends on.
A blue planet, | with surprisingly little water.
